study.title: Proverbs 27 - Wisdom for today, for relationships and for work
study.overview: Proverbs 27 brings together short sayings dealing with humility before the future, moderation in speech, true friendship, prudence in the face of danger, fidelity in work and contentment with enough. The chapter counters the proud self-confidence to God's dependence, the bajulation to useful rebuke, the uncontrolled passion to relational wisdom and greed to concrete satisfaction with what God provides.

outline.title: Humility before tomorrow and passions
outline.explanation: The first proverbs correct the presumption about the future, self-combability and lack of government over strong emotions. Envy appears as a particularly heavy and destructive force, harder to bear than simple anger.

outline.title: Friendship that corrects, comforts and builds
outline.explanation: The section values the frank rebuke, the loyal care of a friend and the sweetness of a sincere council. It also encourages perseverance in the friendships and wisdom of children, who honor parents and responds to critics with a prudent life.

outline.title: Discernment, financial prudence and constancy in serving
outline.explanation: Here the escape of danger on the part of the prudent, the caution in risky commitments, the care of inconvenient words, the persistent domestic conflict and the usefulness of the mutual exercise between friends appear. The text also teaches that fidelity in the work brings fruit and recognition.

outline.title: The revealed heart, the insatiable desire and the value of continuous care
outline.explanation: The chapter concludes by showing that the human heart reflects who the person is, that desires never satiate for themselves and that the person is proved even by praise. Finally, the figure of the shepherd and the farmer illustrates constant diligence: goods and resources can support clothing, field, house and handmaids, but require continuous attention.

study.context: The chapter belongs to the sapiential literature of Proverbs, composed of brief, practical and memorable sayings. The notes provided highlight examples of common life - planning, friendship, agriculture, animal husbandry and family relationships - without requiring detailed historical reconstructions beyond the text itself. The scenario is that of a community in which wisdom is shown in daily life: in speech, in choices, in work and in relationships.
study.theology: The central theological teaching is that human life is limited and dependent on God. It is not up to the human being to boast of tomorrow, as if controlling time or fate. Biblical wisdom appears as humility, prudence and fear of God in practice. The chapter also teaches that the grace of God often comes by concrete means: the faithful correction of a friend, diligence at work, responsibility for the house and the moderation of desires. In contrast, pride, envy, bajulation and covetousness deform the heart. The passage over the heart reflecting the person reinforces that God values interiority, not just appearance. In Protestant evangelical reading, this points to the need for inner transformation and continuous dependence on the Lord, not self-reliance.

scholarViews.insight: The recommendation not to be proud of tomorrow is linked to the fact that human plans only thrive if God wills; therefore, fools act as if they control the future.
The instruction to prefer clear rebuke to hidden love teaches that frank correction can be an act of true care, more useful than affection without sincerity.
The proverb about the man who is wandering from his place is applied to the one who abandons the family and disperses, encountering more problems than what he was looking for.

questions: In which area of my life I act as if tomorrow were under my control, and not under the providence of God?
Do I better receive a friend's sincere correction than empty compliments or bajulation?
Does my way of working, administering resources and caring for the house reveals continuous or carelessness and impulse?
study.practice: This week, choose a concrete practice of Proverbs 27: first, give God a plan that you have treated with anxiety; then ask a mature friend for a sincere observation of your life; finally, review an everyday responsibility - work, finance, home or service - with more attention and constancy. The goal is to live with humility, truth and diligence.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided are partial; therefore, some sentences of the chapter received synthesis without explicit commentary from the authors. The biblical text and comments do not provide enough data to state historical, geographical or linguistic details beyond what has been observed. The mention of "Xeol" and "perdition" in Portuguese was maintained as a traditional translation, without deepening the technical meaning outside the notes available.
